title: Reproduction and Life Cycles
seo_title: Life Sciences 11: Reproduction and Life Cycles Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Organisms reproduce in many ways: mitosis and meiosis, asexual and sexual reproduction, life cycles of plants, fungi and animals, and alternation of generations. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Life Sciences 11)
meta_desc: Free Life Sciences 11 worksheets (BC Curriculum): mitosis, meiosis and life cycles. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

Mitosis makes two identical diploid cells for growth, repair and asexual reproduction. Meiosis makes four genetically different haploid cells (gametes). Crossing over and independent assortment in meiosis, plus random fertilization, create variation.

Plants have alternation of generations: a diploid sporophyte makes spores, and a haploid gametophyte makes gametes. Fungi reproduce with spores; many animals have direct or indirect development (metamorphosis).

Example

A cell has 2n = 8. How many chromosomes are in each gamete?

Haploid: half

Answer: 4

Example

How many cells does meiosis produce from one cell?

Two divisions

Answer: 4

Common mistakes

  • Thinking meiosis makes identical cells.
  • Mixing up haploid and diploid.
  • Thinking fungi make seeds.

faq.a: Homologous chromosomes swap pieces during meiosis, mixing alleles.
It makes variation, so a population can adapt to change.

items.q: What forms the spindle in animal cells?
items.e: Plant cells form a spindle without centrioles.

items.q: In a root tip squash, 24 of 200 cells are in mitosis. Calculate the mitotic index as a percentage.
items.e: Mitotic index = cells in mitosis ÷ total cells × 100 = 12.0%.

items.q: A cell cycle lasts 16 hours. In a sample, 20 of 400 cells are in mitosis. Estimate how long mitosis lasts, in minutes.
items.e: Fraction in mitosis × cycle time = 20/400 × 960 min = 48.0 min.

items.q: In a root tip squash, 36 of 250 cells are in mitosis. Calculate the mitotic index as a percentage.
items.e: Mitotic index = cells in mitosis ÷ total cells × 100 = 14.4%.

items.q: In which stage of the cell cycle does this happen: the cell grows but its DNA does not replicate?
items.e: G₁ phase: the cell grows but its DNA does not replicate.

items.q: What is karyokinesis?
items.e: Cytokinesis follows it.

items.q: A human cell with 46 chromosomes divides by mitosis. How many chromosomes are in both daughter cells together?
items.e: Two cells × 46 = 92.

items.q: A cell cycle lasts 24 hours. In a sample, 20 of 150 cells are in mitosis. Estimate how long mitosis lasts, in minutes.
items.e: Fraction in mitosis × cycle time = 20/150 × 1440 min = 192 min.

items.q: What is the significance of mitosis?
c: growth, repair and keeping the chromosome number the same
creating genetic variation by crossing over
items.e: It replaces worn-out cells.

items.q: A cell cycle lasts 18 hours. In a sample, 15 of 300 cells are in mitosis. Estimate how long mitosis lasts, in minutes.
items.e: Fraction in mitosis × cycle time = 15/300 × 1080 min = 54.0 min.

items.q: A potato cell with 48 chromosomes divides by mitosis. How many chromosomes are in both daughter cells together?
items.e: Two cells × 48 = 96.

items.q: A horse body cell has 64 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in each daughter cell after mitosis?
items.e: Mitosis makes identical cells with the same number.

items.q: What happens in telophase?
c: chromatin condenses into chromosomes and the spindle begins to form
nuclear envelopes and nucleoli re-form round each set of chromosomes
the cell grows but its DNA does not replicate
chromosomes line up at the equator (metaphase plate)

items.q: What happens in anaphase I of meiosis?
c: crossing over takes place at recombination nodules
chiasmata terminalize and the nuclear envelope breaks down
homologous chromosomes pair up (synapsis) to form bivalents
homologous chromosomes separate while sister chromatids stay together
items.e: Anaphase I: homologous chromosomes separate while sister chromatids stay together.

items.q: In which stage of meiosis does this happen: homologous chromosomes pair up (synapsis) to form bivalents?
items.e: Zygotene: homologous chromosomes pair up (synapsis) to form bivalents.

items.q: A potato egg and sperm each have 24 chromosomes. How many does the fertilized egg have?
Which stage of meiosis? Single chromosomes line up in the middle of two cells.
items.e: Meiosis I separates homologs; meiosis II separates sister chromatids.

items.q: A chicken body cell has 78 chromosomes (2n). How many are in each egg or sperm cell?
items.e: Meiosis halves the number: n = 39.

items.q: A fruit fly body cell has 8 chromosomes. How many homologous pairs is that?
items.e: 8 ÷ 2 = 4 pairs.

items.q: Which stage of meiosis? Homologous chromosomes pair up and swap pieces (crossing over).
items.e: Meiosis I separates homologs; meiosis II separates sister chromatids.

items.q: A pea plant egg and sperm each have 7 chromosomes. How many does the fertilized egg have?
A mouse body cell has 40 chromosomes (2n). How many are in each egg or sperm cell?
items.e: Meiosis halves the number: n = 20.

items.q: Which stage of meiosis? Homologous chromosomes separate to opposite poles.
items.e: Meiosis I separates homologs; meiosis II separates sister chromatids.

items.q: In which stage of meiosis does this happen: the synaptonemal complex dissolves and chiasmata are seen?
items.e: Diplotene: the synaptonemal complex dissolves and chiasmata are seen.

items.q: What happens in zygotene of meiosis?
c: homologous chromosomes pair up (synapsis) to form bivalents
the synaptonemal complex dissolves and chiasmata are seen
crossing over takes place at recombination nodules
sister chromatids separate as the centromere splits
items.e: Zygotene: homologous chromosomes pair up (synapsis) to form bivalents.

items.q: Meiosis: number of cells produced?
items.e: Meiosis: four. Mitosis: two.

items.q: A potato body cell has 48 chromosomes (2n). How many are in each egg or sperm cell?
items.e: Meiosis halves the number: n = 24.

items.q: A fruit fly body cell has 8 chromosomes (2n). How many are in each egg or sperm cell?
items.e: Meiosis halves the number: n = 4.

items.q: Mitosis: chromosome number in new cells?
items.e: Meiosis: half (haploid). Mitosis: same (diploid).

items.q: In which stage of meiosis does this happen: crossing over takes place at recombination nodules?
items.e: Pachytene: crossing over takes place at recombination nodules.

items.q: Mitosis: number of cells produced?
items.e: Meiosis: four. Mitosis: two.

items.q: A chimpanzee body cell has 48 chromosomes (2n). How many are in each egg or sperm cell?
items.e: Meiosis halves the number: n = 24.

items.q: In which stage of meiosis does this happen: homologous chromosomes separate while sister chromatids stay together?
items.e: Anaphase I: homologous chromosomes separate while sister chromatids stay together.

items.q: A colour-blind man and a woman who is not a carrier have a son. What is the chance the son is colour-blind?
c: 0, because the son gets his X chromosome from his mother
items.e: Fathers pass their Y to sons.

items.q: A diploid cell of a species of fruit fly has 10 chromosomes. How many different combinations of chromosomes can its gametes have by independent segregation?
items.e: With n = 5 pairs, combinations = 2n = 32.

items.q: A horse egg and sperm each have 32 chromosomes. How many does the fertilized egg have?
What is codominance?
c: both alleles are fully expressed in the heterozygote, such as blood group AB
items.e: Incomplete dominance gives a blend, such as pink flowers.

items.q: What is the phenotype of an organism?
c: its observable characteristics, produced by genotype and environment
the DNA sequence of one gene
items.e: Genotype + environment → phenotype.

items.q: What is an allele?
c: a section of a chromosome with many genes
a different form of the same gene
items.e: For example, alleles for blood group A, B and O.

items.q: Which is a polygenic trait?
items.e: Many genes plus environment give continuous variation.

items.q: A chicken body cell has 78 chromosomes. How many homologous pairs is that?
What is non-disjunction?
c: chromosomes failing to separate in meiosis, giving gametes with an extra or missing chromosome
items.e: Trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) can result.

items.q: Why are sex-linked recessive conditions such as red–green colour blindness more common in males?
c: males have one X chromosome, so a single recessive allele is expressed
the allele is on the Y chromosome
items.e: Females need two copies to show the trait.

items.q: A diploid cell of a fungus has 46 chromosomes. How many different combinations of chromosomes can its gametes have by independent segregation?
items.e: With n = 23 pairs, combinations = 2n = 8388608.

items.q: A species has 3 pairs of chromosomes. How many different chromosome combinations can occur in zygotes from random fertilization (ignoring crossing over)?
A species has 4 pairs of chromosomes. How many different chromosome combinations can occur in zygotes from random fertilization (ignoring crossing over)?
A chimpanzee body cell has 48 chromosomes. How many homologous pairs is that?
A chicken egg and sperm each have 39 chromosomes. How many does the fertilized egg have?
In a pedigree, two unaffected parents have an affected child. What does this show?
c: the trait is recessive and both parents are carriers
items.e: A dominant trait would show in a parent.

items.q: A pea plant body cell has 14 chromosomes (2n). How many are in each egg or sperm cell?
items.e: Meiosis halves the number: n = 7.

items.q: How does meiosis produce genetic variation?
c: by crossing over and independent assortment of homologous chromosomes
items.e: Random fertilization adds more variation.

items.q: What does homozygous mean?
c: having two identical alleles of a gene
items.e: BB and bb are homozygous.

items.q: What is the expected ratio of phenotypes from a cross between two heterozygotes (Aa × Aa) for a dominant trait?
items.e: The genotype ratio is 1 AA : 2 Aa : 1 aa.

items.q: To which class of fungi do mushrooms, bracket fungi and smuts belong?
items.e: Basidiomycetes: mushrooms, bracket fungi and smuts.

items.q: To which class of fungi do Alternaria and Trichoderma belong?
items.e: Deuteromycetes: Alternaria and Trichoderma.

items.q: Which group of plants is described as pteridophytes?
c: the first land plants with vascular tissue (xylem and phloem)
the amphibians of the plant kingdom
flowering plants with seeds enclosed in fruits
plants with naked seeds, not enclosed in an ovary
items.e: The first land plants with vascular tissue (xylem and phloem): pteridophytes.

items.q: Which fungi belong to Phycomycetes?
items.e: Phycomycetes: Rhizopus and Albugo.

items.q: Which plants are called the amphibians of the plant kingdom?
items.e: The amphibians of the plant kingdom: bryophytes.

items.q: What is a haplontic life cycle?
c: the sporophyte is only the one-celled zygote; the gametophyte is dominant
items.e: Seen in Volvox, Spirogyra and some Chlamydomonas.

items.q: In which group do vascular tissues first appear?
items.e: They have true roots, stems and leaves.

items.q: Which is the dominant phase of the life cycle in bryophytes?
items.e: The sporophyte grows on the gametophyte.

items.q: Which plants are called plants with naked seeds, not enclosed in an ovary?

items.q: Which algae have the pigment fucoxanthin?
items.e: It gives the olive-green to brown colour.

items.q: What is the protonema?

items.q: What is heterospory?
